claim: For \(\Omega_{5/2}=(-1,1)\cup(3/2,7/2)\cup(-7/2,-3/2)\), the Turán constant is exactly \[\mathcal T_{\mathbb R}(\Omega_{5/2})=\frac{(2a+1)^2(4a^2-6a+1)^2}{128a^6-20a^2+5}=2.1353071788763974322\ldots,\] where \(a\) is the unique zero in \((0.53305,0.53306)\) of \(256a^7+256a^6-96a^5-80a^4+40a^3+30a^2-15a-5\). Equivalently, \(\mathcal T_{\mathbb Z}(\{0,\pm1,\pm4,\pm5,\pm6\})\) is twice this value. An explicit nonnegative square-cubic trigonometric polynomial attains the lower bound, while a positive three-node dual quadrature supported at its three zeros gives the matching upper bound.
integrity: The proof supplies both a primal nonnegative polynomial and a positive dual quadrature with matching objective. The included exact-rational checker verifies the algebraic identities and sign brackets; its decimal output is illustrative and is not used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The exact evaluation is only for the parameter \(\lambda=5/2\); no classification of other rational parameters is claimed. A residual literature risk is that the identical finite Carathéodory–Fejér constant may have appeared under different notation in older tables.
title: Exact Turán constant at \(\lambda=5/2\)
